input.quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
input.rationale: Section 21 meets the preferred position in full. §21.1 imposes a mutual aggregate cap at the greater of Fees paid or payable in the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000, and "Fees" (§1.5) captures recurring subscription, professional services and usage fees, so the cap is not illusory. §21.2 excludes indirect and consequential damages mutually (with helpful direct-damage carve-ins for Customer Data restoration and incident response). §21.3 defines "Excluded Claims" — confidentiality, data-protection and security breaches, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other Party's IP — and because both §21.1 and §21.2 open "Except for Excluded Claims", those categories sit wholly outside the cap with no super-cap elsewhere in the document. §21.3 also confirms Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees is not damages and is not limited by the Section. §19.5 and §21.4 reinforce that indemnity, confidentiality and data-protection duties are not cut down. No redline required.
